User's display name for community identification and author attribution in discussions.

This name appears as the author byline on articles and is used for community identification throughout the discussion board. It provides the primary means for other users to recognize and reference the author within community interactions and content attribution contexts.

avatar_url.description:
Optional profile picture URL for visual user identification in community interfaces.

Displayed alongside the user's name in list views, search results, and community features to help users quickly identify authors and community members. The image enhances community interaction by providing visual context for user contributions and discussions.

status.description:
User account status indicating current participation level and community interaction permissions.

This status determines the user's visibility to other community members, their ability to publish content, and their general participation capabilities within the discussion board. Status affects community directory listings and interaction features.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionUser.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching and filtering discussion board users.

Provides comprehensive search and filtering capabilities for user management and community features within the economic and political discussion platform. This schema supports multiple filtering strategies including text-based search across user profiles, status-based filtering, and temporal filtering by account creation dates.

The search functionality enables efficient user discovery through partial name matching and case-insensitive searches across display names and user biographies. This is particularly valuable for community management, user verification, and participant identification in discussion threads.

Pagination parameters ensure optimal performance when handling large user lists, with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Results are always returned in paginated format to maintain system performance and provide a smooth user experience for administrators managing community participation.

All parameters are optional and can be combined for sophisticated search scenarios, allowing administrators to build complex user queries for moderation, analytics, and community engagement purposes.

page.description:
Page number for pagination. Defaults to 1 for the first page of results.

Controls which subset of filtered users to retrieve from the complete result set. Page numbering starts at 1, allowing for intuitive navigation through search results. Combined with the limit parameter, this provides flexible control over result retrieval for both performance optimization and user interface design.

Used primarily by front-end applications to implement paginated user lists and by administrative interfaces to efficiently navigate through large user bases without overwhelming system resources.

limit.description:
Number of users to return per page. Maximum 100 users per request for performance.

Controls the size of each page in the paginated results. Setting appropriate limits helps balance between providing sufficient user information and maintaining system performance. The maximum limit of 100 users prevents excessive data transfer and processing that could impact application responsiveness.

Commonly used for user list displays, administrative user management interfaces, and bulk user operations where multiple user records need to be processed simultaneously.

search.description:
Text search across user display names and biographies. Performs case-insensitive partial matching.

Enables keyword-based user discovery by searching across both the user's display name and their biographical information. The search is case-insensitive and supports partial matching, allowing users to find participants even with incomplete search terms or alternative spellings.

This functionality is essential for community features where users need to locate specific participants in discussions, for administrative user management where staff need to quickly find user accounts, and for community engagement scenarios where users want to discover participants with similar interests.

status.description:
Filter users by account status. Common values include 'active', 'suspended', 'deactivated'.

Provides filtering based on user account lifecycle states to support various administrative and community management scenarios. Active accounts represent fully participating community members, suspended accounts indicate temporary restrictions, and deactivated accounts represent either user-initiated deactivation or administrative suspension.

This filtering is crucial for moderation workflows, community health monitoring, and administrative oversight where different account states require different levels of interaction and management approaches.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionArticle.description:
Core discussion articles for economic and political topics.

Represents the primary content structure for fostering meaningful discourse about economic policies, political developments, market analysis, and related topics within the discussion platform. Each article serves as an independent discussion thread that enables users to create, edit, and engage with content that matters to the community.

The article system supports comprehensive content creation through rich text capabilities, allowing for detailed analysis, opinion pieces, data presentations, and collaborative discussions. The categorization system provides organizational structure, enabling users to navigate discussions by specific topics such as 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', 'Market Discussion', or 'Regulatory Updates'.

Content lifecycle management is built into the article system, with full temporal tracking for creation, modification, and soft deletion capabilities. This ensures content preservation for historical reference while allowing for community moderation and content management. The platform maintains referential integrity and supports attachment relationships for comprehensive multimedia discussions.

Each article establishes a clear author relationship through the econ_political_discussion_users relationship, providing proper attribution and user accountability. The system supports multiple file attachments through the attachment management subsystem, enabling users to share relevant documents, images, charts, and other supporting materials that enhance the discussion quality.

id.description:
Primary key identifier for the discussion article.

Unique UUID-based identifier that serves as the primary key for article records in the database. This identifier is automatically generated when the article is created and remains constant throughout the article's lifecycle, providing a reliable reference point for all article-related operations including updates, deletions, and attachment associations.

title.description:
Article title for the discussion post. Descriptive topic heading that summarizes the main discussion point.

Provides a concise but descriptive heading that captures the essence of the discussion topic. The title serves as the primary identifier in article lists, search results, and social sharing scenarios. Well-crafted titles help users quickly understand the article's focus and encourage engagement from community members interested in the specific topic area.

content.description:
Full article content for the economic/political discussion. Rich text content body containing the detailed discussion post.

Contains the complete discussion content including text, formatting, and embedded media. This field supports rich content creation for detailed analysis, opinion pieces, data presentations, and collaborative discussions. The content serves as the primary vehicle for knowledge sharing and community engagement within the economic and political discourse platform.

category.description:
Topic category for economic/political classification such as 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', 'Market Discussion', or 'Regulatory Updates'.

Provides organizational classification for discussions, enabling users to browse content by specific topic areas and helping with content discovery. Categories support natural organization of discussions and help users find content relevant to their interests or expertise areas. Common categories include but are not limited to Economic Policy, Political Analysis, Market Discussion, Regulatory Updates, International Relations, and Social Economics.

status.description:
Article publication status indicating whether the discussion is 'published', 'draft', 'archived', or 'hidden'.

Controls the visibility and interaction capabilities of the article within the platform. Published articles are visible and interactive for all users, draft articles are only visible to the author and administrators, archived articles are preserved but removed from active browsing, and hidden articles are temporarily removed from public view pending review or moderation.

econ_political_discussion_user_id.description:
Author who created this article discussion. Foreign key reference to econ_political_discussion_users.id.

References the user account that created this discussion article, establishing authorship and accountability. This foreign key relationship ensures referential integrity and enables proper attribution for all content created within the platform. The relationship supports user accountability and enables community features such as author profile linking and content moderation workflows.

author.description:
Author information for this discussion article. Contains user identification and display name for proper attribution.

Provides complete author identification information including the user's display name and unique identifier. This reference enables proper attribution display in article interfaces, supports community features like author profile linking, and provides the foundation for author-based content filtering and user engagement tracking throughout the discussion platform.

attachments.description:
File and image attachments associated with this discussion article. Includes images, documents, and other files uploaded by the author.

Contains all file attachments that have been uploaded to complement the discussion content. Attachments enhance the discussion by providing supporting documents, charts, images, and other relevant materials. Each attachment includes comprehensive metadata including security scanning status, moderation status, and access control information to ensure safe and appropriate file sharing within the community.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when this discussion article was originally created.

Records the exact date and time when the article was initially created in the system. This timestamp is automatically set by the system and cannot be modified, providing an immutable record of when the discussion was initiated. The timestamp is used for chronological ordering, content archival, and community activity tracking.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this discussion article was last modified.

Tracks the most recent modification time for the article content, providing users and administrators with information about content recency and ensuring transparency about content changes. This timestamp is automatically updated whenever the article content, title, category, or status is modified.

deleted_at.description:
Soft delete timestamp for archived or removed discussions. Null for active discussions.

Indicates when the article was soft-deleted from the system, providing content recovery capabilities and maintaining referential integrity. Articles with a null deleted_at value are active and visible to users, while articles with a timestamp value have been removed from public view but remain in the database for recovery, archival, and compliance purposes.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionArticle.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new discussion article.

Used for posting new economic and political discussion content. Includes all user-provided fields for article creation with proper validation and content structure.

Author information is automatically derived from the authenticated user's session context and cannot be manually specified. System-managed fields like timestamps are automatically populated during creation. Articles are created with 'published' status by default unless otherwise specified.

Supports optional file attachments that can be uploaded simultaneously with article creation for complete discussion thread setup, though this is not required for successful article creation.

title.description: Article title for the discussion post. Should be descriptive and summarize the main topic or question being discussed.

content.description: Full article content for the economic/political discussion. Rich text content body containing the detailed discussion post, analysis, or commentary.

category.description: Topic category for economic/political classification. Common categories include 'Economic Policy', 'Political Analysis', 'Market Discussion', 'Regulatory Updates', 'International Relations', or 'Social Economics'.

status.description: Article publication status. Defaults to 'published' for immediate visibility, can be set to 'draft' for review before posting.

econ_political_discussion_user_id.description: Unique identifier of the user creating this article. Automatically derived from authenticated session context and cannot be manually specified.

attachments.description: Optional file and image attachments to be uploaded with this article. Supports atomic creation where attachments are uploaded simultaneously with article creation, eliminating the need for separate upload operations. Not required for successful article creation.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionArticle.IUpdate.description:
Request body for updating existing discussion articles.

Allows modification of article content, title, category, and status. Preserves authorship and creation timestamp while updating article metadata and content.

Only the fields that need to be updated should be included in the request. Unspecified fields will retain their current values. Author identification is automatically derived from the authenticated user's session and cannot be manipulated through this request.

Supports soft delete operations through the deleted_at field. When this field is set, the article becomes archived but remains in the system for historical reference.

title.description: Updated article title for the discussion post. Can be modified to better reflect the content or focus of the discussion.

content.description: Updated full article content for the economic/political discussion. Can be used to edit, expand, or clarify the discussion content.

category.description: Updated topic category for economic/political classification. Can be changed to better categorize the discussion topic.

status.description: Updated article publication status. Can be used to publish drafts, archive active discussions, or hide content for moderation.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp for archiving or removing discussions. Set to archive content while preserving historical data. Null for active discussions.

Contains essential article information optimized for display in discussion lists, search results, and category browsing. Excludes full content and attachments for performance.

Includes basic metadata while maintaining efficient list rendering performance.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionAttachment.description:
File and image attachments for economic and political discussion articles.

Stores uploaded files and images that users attach to their discussion posts, supporting rich media content in economic and political discourse. Each attachment includes comprehensive metadata for file management, security scanning, and content moderation.

Supports multiple file types including images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP up to 5MB) and documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT up to 10MB). Files are associated with specific discussion articles and include security scanning status and access controls.

The table maintains file metadata including original filename, MIME type, file size, and storage URL. All attachments are subject to content moderation and security scanning before becoming publicly accessible.

Attachments remain associated with articles even if original content is modified, providing historical context and supporting comprehensive discussion threads with multimedia content.

id.description: Unique primary key identifier for the file attachment. Generated automatically using UUID v4 format when the attachment is created in the system.

article.description: Reference to the discussion article this attachment belongs to. Provides complete article context for attachment management, display, and navigation between article and associated files.

original_filename.description: Original filename as uploaded by the user. Preserves the user's original file naming convention for reference, identification, and file management purposes. Used in download responses and file listing interfaces.

file_type.description: MIME type or file extension indicating the type of file such as 'image/jpeg', 'application/pdf', 'text/plain'. Determines how the file should be handled, displayed, and what applications can open it.

file_size.description: File size in bytes for storage management and bandwidth tracking. Used for storage utilization monitoring, upload validation, and display purposes in file management interfaces.

file_url.description: URL or path where the file is stored in the cloud storage system. Direct access link for file retrieval, download, and display. Should be a publicly accessible URL for public files or authenticated URL for restricted files.

upload_date.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded to the system using ISO 8601 format. Used for chronological ordering, recency indication, and audit trail purposes.

uploader_name.description: Name of the user who uploaded the file for attribution and contact purposes. Used in user interfaces to show who uploaded each file and for accountability when issues arise.

security_scan_status.description: Status of security scanning indicating file safety assessment. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting scan), 'clean' (no threats detected), 'flagged' (potential issues found), 'quarantined' (threat detected and isolated).

moderation_status.description: Content moderation status for file appropriateness evaluation. Valid values: 'pending' (awaiting review), 'approved' (deemed appropriate), 'rejected' (deemed inappropriate), 'requires_review' (needs manual review).

is_public.description: Whether this file is publicly accessible or restricted to authorized users only. Controls access permissions and determines if file can be viewed by anonymous users or requires authentication.

Request body for uploading a new file attachment to a discussion article.

Used for adding files and images to existing discussion articles. Supports both direct file upload and pre-uploaded file references for flexibility in file management workflows.

File size limits depend on file type: images (JPG, PNG, GIF, WebP) up to 5MB, documents (PDF, DOC, DOCX, TXT) up to 10MB. All uploads undergo automatic security scanning and content moderation before becoming publicly accessible.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionAttachment.ISumm.description:
Attachment summary information for discussion article media files.

This object represents essential file and media information for attachments associated with economic and political discussion articles. It provides the core metadata needed for content identification, security assessment, and access control within the discussion platform.

The attachment summary includes unique identification through attachment ID, which enables precise file referencing and access control operations. Original filename provides human-readable identification for file management and user interface display purposes. These fields form the essential file identity information required for basic media content interaction.

File type classification and MIME type specification provide technical information about the attachment format, enabling proper content handling, security assessment, and user interface adaptation. File size information supports storage management, bandwidth planning, and user experience optimization by indicating potential loading times and bandwidth requirements.

Upload timestamp and uploader information provide historical context about attachment provenance and accountability. Uploader identification supports community responsibility, content attribution, and moderation workflows when issues arise with specific files.

Security scan status indicates the current security assessment of the file, determining whether the attachment is safe for public access or requires additional review. This field supports platform security by filtering potentially harmful content and protecting users from malicious files.

Moderation status indicates the current approval state of the attachment content, determining public accessibility and visibility within discussion threads. This field supports content quality assurance and community guidelines enforcement by controlling when and how attachments appear in discussions.

Public accessibility status determines whether the attachment is viewable by all platform users or restricted to specific user groups or article participants. This field supports privacy controls and content sharing management for sensitive or restricted media content.

Storage information including file URL or storage path enables direct access to the attachment content when authorized. Security considerations ensure that file access is properly controlled based on user permissions and content visibility settings.

This summary format balances information visibility with security protection, providing sufficient detail for content interaction while maintaining appropriate access controls and privacy protections. The summary structure integrates with the full attachment management system to enable progressive content disclosure based on user relationships and authorization levels.

Used in attachment list displays, media galleries, search results, and content management interfaces where detailed file information is necessary but complete technical specifications are not required.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionContentModerator.description:
Content moderator registration request structure for creating new moderator accounts with elevated permissions.

Contains all necessary information for establishing a new content moderator account including authentication credentials, profile details, and session context information. This schema supports the platform's moderator onboarding process while maintaining security requirements and proper account setup.

Session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are included to establish proper security monitoring and session tracking for moderator account creation. The registration process creates a new moderator with default 'active' status and appropriate permissions for content management functions.

Used in moderator account creation operations, supporting secure onboarding of qualified content moderators with proper authorization and account setup procedures.

Authenticated content moderator response with JWT tokens and session information.

This schema represents the complete authentication response for content moderators after successful login or token refresh. It contains the moderator's identity information, security tokens, and session context needed for subsequent API interactions.

The authorized response provides access credentials for content moderation functions including content oversight, community management, user interaction monitoring, and administrative controls throughout the discussion board platform. This response establishes the moderator's authenticated session with appropriate permissions and role context.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated content moderator account. This UUID serves as the primary identifier for the moderator within the system and is used for authorization checks, audit trails, and moderator-specific operations throughout the platform.

display_name.description: Content moderator's display name used for identification and attribution across the discussion platform. Appears with moderation actions and system notifications.

email.description: Email address of the authenticated content moderator. This is the same email used during login and serves as the moderator's account identifier for communication and system notifications related to moderation activities.

bio.description: Optional moderator biography describing expertise, background, or moderation approach. Provides context for community trust and user understanding.

avatar_url.description: Optional profile picture URL for moderator identification in discussions and moderation dashboards. Supports visual recognition of moderation actions.

status.description: Content moderator account status indicating current operational state: 'active' for full moderation access, 'suspended' for temporary restrictions, or 'inactive' for dormant accounts.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this moderator account was originally created. Used for audit trails and account lifecycle tracking.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this moderator profile was last updated. Reflects latest changes to account information or settings.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp for deactivated moderator accounts. Present only for deleted accounts, null for active or suspended moderators.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionContentModerator.description:
Content moderator login credentials for authentication in the economic and political discussion board system.

This schema represents the required authentication information for content moderators to access the platform's moderation dashboard and content management tools. The login process validates moderator credentials against stored account information and establishes a secure session with JWT token generation for subsequent API calls.

Moderators use this credential type to authenticate for content oversight, community management, and administrative functions throughout the discussion board platform. Failed authentication attempts are tracked for security monitoring and rate-limiting protection.

email.description: Content moderator email address used for account authentication. Must be a valid email address that matches the registered moderator account in the system. This email serves as the primary identifier for moderator authentication and is validated against the stored account information.

password.description: Content moderator password for account authentication. Must match the stored password hash for the specified email address. Password is transmitted in plain text during login and validated against the secure hash stored in the database. Password should meet security requirements for moderator account access.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Optional field that provides additional context for session creation and audit trail maintenance. When provided, helps with geographic session tracking and security analysis. Server can extract this information automatically if not provided by the client.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) for session context and audit trail. Mandatory field that provides the URL of the page from which the login request originates. This information is essential for session tracking, user experience analysis, and security monitoring purposes.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) for session context and audit trail. Mandatory field that provides the URL of the page that referred to the login page. This information helps track user navigation patterns and supports security analysis for session creation context.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionContentModerator.description:
Refresh token request for session renewal in the content moderation system.

This schema enables content moderators to extend their authenticated session without requiring re-authentication. The refresh mechanism validates the provided refresh token against stored session data and generates new access tokens with extended expiration periods.

Moderators use this token refresh process to maintain continuous access to content management tools, moderation dashboard, and administrative functions during extended work sessions. Security protocols ensure refresh tokens are single-use with automatic rotation upon successful renewal.

refreshToken.description: Valid refresh token for session renewal. Must be a valid, non-expired refresh token that was issued during the initial authentication process. This token is used to validate the moderator's continued access rights and generate new access tokens with extended session lifetime.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionContentModerator.description:
Password reset request for content moderator accounts.

Used to initiate password recovery for content moderator accounts when access is forgotten or compromised. This request type enables secure password restoration through email verification by sending time-limited reset tokens to the registered content moderator email address.

The request contains minimal required information to validate moderator account existence and trigger the password reset workflow. Reset tokens are cryptographically generated with secure randomness and expire after 24 hours for security. This process ensures moderator account integrity while providing essential account recovery capabilities.

Content moderators use this type to request password resets when they cannot access their accounts due to forgotten credentials or suspected compromise.

email.description:
Content moderator email address used for password reset verification.

Must match the registered email address in the econ_political_discussion_users table for the content moderator account. This email will receive the password reset token and instructions for account recovery.

Email validation ensures password reset requests can only be initiated for existing moderator accounts. The system validates email existence before generating reset tokens to prevent unnecessary token generation for non-existent accounts.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionContentModerator.description:
Password reset confirmation response for content moderator accounts.

Returned after successful password reset request initiation for content moderator accounts. This response confirms the reset process has been started and provides next steps for the moderator to complete password restoration.

The response includes confirmation that reset tokens have been generated and instructions for accessing password reset emails. It guides content moderators through the secure password restoration process, ensuring they understand the next steps required to set new passwords.

Content moderators receive this confirmation after password reset requests and use the information to complete their account recovery through email-based token validation.

message.description:
Password reset confirmation message for content moderator.

Provides clear confirmation that the password reset request has been processed successfully. This message informs the moderator that password reset instructions have been sent to their registered email address.

The confirmation message is designed to reassure content moderators that their password reset request was successful and provide clear next steps. It may include specific timing information for email delivery and token expiration.

Content moderators rely on this message to understand that their password reset request was successful and that they should check their email for reset instructions.

next_steps.description:
Next steps instructions for content moderator password reset.

Provides detailed guidance on the password reset process completion steps. This includes information about email timing, token usage, and password setting requirements.

The next steps typically include instructions to check email for reset tokens, token expiration timing (24 hours), and password complexity requirements (8+ characters, mixed case, numbers, special characters) for setting new passwords.

Content moderators use these instructions to successfully complete their password reset process and restore access to their moderator accounts.

email_sent.description:
Indicates whether password reset email was successfully sent.

Boolean flag confirming that the password reset email with token was successfully generated and sent to the content moderator's registered email address.

This field provides explicit confirmation of email delivery status, allowing content moderators to understand whether they should expect password reset instructions in their email. If false, it may indicate an email delivery issue requiring support intervention.

Content moderators can rely on this flag to verify email delivery status and take appropriate action if email delivery failed.

email.description: User email address used for account authentication and login credentials.

password.description: User password for account authentication. Must match the stored password hash for the account.

ip.description: Client IP address for session tracking and security monitoring. Optional field that server can extract from request headers.

href.description: Connection URL (current page URL) for session context and navigation tracking. Mandatory field for session management.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (previous page URL) for session context and navigation tracking. Mandatory field for session management.

IEconPoliticalDiscussionUser.ILogin.description:
User login request credentials and session context for economic and political discussion platform authentication.

Contains the required authentication information for existing users to access their accounts in the discussion platform. This DTO enables registered users to authenticate and establish secure sessions for platform access and article creation activities.

The login process validates email and password credentials against stored user accounts, then generates secure session tokens for authorized access. Session context information including connection URL, referrer URL, and optional IP address support security monitoring and session management requirements.

All associated articles automatically reflect category updates while maintaining their original publication status, engagement metrics, and user access permissions.
